newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Merger news awaited from Royal&Sun.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Merger news awaited from Royal&Sun.

text.p: Britain's largest composite insurer, Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc next Thursday reports its first set of annual figures since its creation in a six billion stg merger last year.
Questions on how the integration of Royal Insurance and Sun Alliance Insurance is going and how succesful cost cutting has been are likely to top the agenda on Thursday.
Analysts have little to go on other than the company's own forecasts last July and earlier this year a spokesman for the company said that its initial cost cutting targets might be exceeded.
The company has identified cost savings of around 175 million stg by 1998, with about 60 percent of the savings coming from the shedding of some 5,000 jobs.

"Most people are factoring in at least 175 million stg now and maybe a bit more. Clearly almost a year into the merger it'll be quite important to have some more information on how fast those costs are being cut and how smoothly the integration is going," said one analyst.
Plans have already been announced to close around 100 branches, reduce head count by 1,300 and cut the six London offices to three.
Analysts are expecting a restructuring charge of between 150 and 175 million stg.
For the year, the market expects profits of around 859 million stg and a dividend for the year of 19 pence per share.
At the half-year stage, Royal & Sun produced substantially better than expected results, with a fall in operating profits to 450 million stg.

Worldwide weather-related claims of 94 million stg were one factor then and that theme has been repeated in results released by both Commercial Union and Guardian Royal Exchange (GRE) earlier this week.
Both those companies also blamed stiff competition, particulary in the UK general insurance market for sharp falls in profits over the past 12 months.
Royal & Sun's solvency ratio - the value of assets as a proportion of premium income - will be another focus of attention next week.

In July, that ratio was around 73 percent - high by industry standards and largely inherited from Sun Alliance. The worry is that over time it will dilute the return on equity and there have been suggestions it should consider a share buyback.

GRE's which has also seen its solvency ratio climb over the past year, earlier this week rejected calls to return capital to shareholders saying they were looking to make an acquisition, possibly in the life sector.

Royal & Sun's response is likely to be 'wait and see' with the company reluctant to give capital back until the consolidation of operations is further down the line and it sees how the non-life cycle develops.
Also likely to be on people's minds is the possibility that Royal & Sun is looking for acquisitions.

"Clearly while the reorganisation is going on an acquisition is likely to be later rather than sooner. Having said that the way prices are moving in UK life, maybe it simply can't afford to wait," said an analyst.
"I think it would like to strengthen its position in life generally. While its name hasn't been mentioned in relation to acquistions in UK life, they must be thinking about it."
Royal & Sun may also be copnsidering strengthening its position in continental Europe through a life acquisition, he added.
-- Simon Cowell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7721
